title.ph: Meet Cerberus: A Puppy with Big Drive!

concept.shortdesc: Hi, I'm Cerberus, a 10-month-old German Shepherd–Boxer mix! I'm an energetic and intelligent working dog breed looking for my forever home. If you enjoy working with intelligent, responsive, and energetic dogs, then Cerberus may be an ideal fit. Please read through this PDF guide to see if we're a good match!

section.title: Dog Details

ul.li: Allergies: None officially, but sneezes and itches frequently (testing allergy chews)

section.p: You can view the full, official health and vaccination record here (requires permission from foster agent):

ul.li: Human presence during most of the day
Toys and games that challenge his mind

section.title: Feeding and Grooming Habits
section.p: Cerberus eats well and responds to food as a training tool. He enjoys a steady routine and a balanced diet.

ul.li: Two meals daily of dry kibble
Likes yogurt, peanut butter, broths, and watermelon
Needs weekly coat and teeth brushing

section.title: Temperament and Activity
section.p: Cerberus is alert, affectionate, and playful. He builds bonds quickly and shows joy when given shared tasks.

ul.li: Needs structured walks and mental games
Enjoys treat balls, squeaky toys, beach balls

section.title: Socialization
section.p: Cerberus connects deeply and thrives in homes with structure. He values routine, activity, and companionship.

ul.li: Trained to give hugs, doesn’t jump up
Pack-oriented; enjoys daycare and dog companions

section.note: He is not suited for homes with cats, chaotic energy, or owners seeking a low-energy pet.

section.title: Training Needs
section.p: Cerberus shows strong potential and benefits from structured, positive reinforcement.

ul.li: Currently in formal training with Lydia Register (AAS, CPDT-KA)
High prey drive (squirrels, rabbits, small dogs)

section.note: Lydia Register will offer discounted training sessions to Cerberus's future adopter.

ul.li: Good match: Remote or hybrid worker; active adult or couple; retiree with routine
Not a good match: High-traffic or chaotic home; confined living space (i.e., apartment)

section.title: Please Contact Christina Mayr for Adoption Details:
section.p: If Cerberus sounds like a good fit for your home or foster program, please explore the full adoption package, and contact Christina Mayr, the foster coordinator. She’ll follow up shortly to begin the conversation!

reference.shortdesc: This reference answers the most common questions about preparing your home for Cerberus.

section.title: Q: Do I need a house with a yard to adopt Cerberus?
section.p: A: Yes, Cerberus is best suited to houses with backyards to allow him to meet his daily activity needs.

section.title: Q: How long can Cerberus be left alone?
section.p: A: He should not be left alone for more than 4–5 hours without a break.

section.title: Q: Does Cerberus need a crate?
section.p: A: Yes. Cerberus can tolerate crates and occasionally sleep in crates with appropriate encouragement. A soft-sided crate or a quiet “safe area” can be used for short rest periods, but a gated room or playpen is often a better option.

section.title: Q: Can Cerberus live with cats or other small pets?
section.p: A: No, Cerberus is not compatible with cats and has a strong prey drive. Small pets must have fully secure enclosures and be closely supervised if they are in the same home. Cerberus will likely do well with a calm, balanced dog after slow, careful introductions. Success depends on the other dog’s temperament and the adopter’s ability to manage the process.

section.title: Q: How do I introduce Cerberus to children?
section.p: A: Cerberus does best in adult-only homes or with children over five years old. Always supervise interactions, teach children to respect Cerberus's space, and avoid hugging or rough play.

section.title: Q: How should I handle visitors coming to my home?
section.p: A: Cerberus can be protective of his space. Keep him leashed or behind a gate during arrivals and reward calm behavior as guests enter. Give him time to adjust at his own pace.

section.title: Q: Who can I reach out to for adoption or training details and questions?
section.p: A: For training information, please contact Lydia Registar (AAS, CPDT-KA).
For adoption questions, please contact Christina Mayr or Ruby Leonaraine
